== ''Recommended Mods'' ==
<u>Scape and Run: Parasites is not balanced for a vanilla-only experience, so it's recommended to have a few more mods installed.</u><br>
If you're having trouble dealing with parasites, try installing some of the mods listed below.

{|class="fandom-table mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" style="width: 750px"
|+
'''Advice For Certain [[Evolution Phases|Phases]]'''
!Phases
!Advice For Phase
|-
|Phase 0
|
*[[Buglin|Buglins]] will spawn naturally during Phase 0 so it is highly recommended to kill on sight.
*Buglins take 75 seconds to evolve into [[Rupter|Rupters]]. When it's just one, all they will do is infect and run away from the player, killing on sight is highly recommended, however if you encounter more than one, they will start attacking you so your main focus in Phase 0 is to prepare and get a weapon and shield.
*Buglins will apply [[Call Of The Hive]] when touched and the effect can stack so be cautious.
|-
|Phase 1
|
*Rupters will now spawn naturally during this phase and will attack players and mobs instead of infecting by CotH cloud so try avoiding these creepy crawlies, especially their variants because they can be more dangerous than most Assimilated mobs due to their speed, the effects they give, and their leaping capabilities.
*Parasites will now ignore sky light levels when spawning so the surface is now equally dangerous.
*Sleeping adds 40 points now so sleeping exactly 20 days (gaining 800 points) would put you in Phase 2, but half the points gained would be due to the parasites themselves so expect 10 minimum sleepings before going into Phase 2.
*Since Rupters spawn now, having defenses around your base that prevents climbing parasites would be ideal. I'd suggest fences along with Barbed Wire from the Nuclear Tech Mod in order to damage these guys, however loot will not drop if they die from it.
*If you haven't been using Lava or Fire yet, now would be a good time.
*Use anything at your disposal to fight back from here forward because your main goal here is to survive.
|-
|Phase 2
|
|}

==Tips And Tricks==
*If it isn't obvious already, use fire. Especially against Primitive parasites and above, Fire Aspect is a must (especially since most [[:Category:Weapons|Weapons]] added by the mod won't benefit from other enchantments) and lava is good against stationary parasites.
*If you're using the Nuclear Tech Mod (Extended Edition) you can use the Null Grenade as a last resort. This kills everything, including dangerous tiers like Adapted, Pure, Nexus, Preeminent, and even Derived, without exceptions. The only downside is that you won't get any loot and if you're in the 7x7 area you will die. Thank you Boiledlawyer9883 for getting the info for me.
*From the Nuclear Tech mod again, the "F.L.E.I.J.A" nuke will delete anything within a 50-block radius in a sphere shape which makes for another good last resort if needed. Thank you again Boiledlawyer9883. However The Prototype nuke is the same way but 150 block radius.
*Incendiary Grenades are good for taking down Beckons (AS LONG AS WATER ISN'T IN THE MIX), on the other hand Flaming Barbed Wire is good for Adapted parasites and below.
*Sky bases are also good with the right resources and blocks, coward's way out maybe but who cares you're living.
*Break Dispatcher Nidus blocks and any Parasitic Cyst on the ground. This will prevent Dispatchers from spawning and prevent points from being gained faster due to Cysts consuming items.
*NEVER leave a Dispatcher to live unless you want to have Sentries spawning all over the place.
*Try using multiple traps at once around your base so parasites can't adapt to it all. (Ex: Flaming Barbed Wire + Electric Fence + Turrets + Firing guns from above + Lava + Iron Golems + Grenades) Adapted parasites can adapt up to 8 damage sources so lots of traps and damage outputs would be efficient and overwhelm most parasites.
*If you want, make hitboxes show by pressing F3+b. This is particularly needed to hit the tendrils of adapted parasites or above, as the tendril hitboxes are easy to miss or distinguish, and may be displaced sometimes.
*Kill anything that drops food early on, so you have food to support a long run.<ref>Do this to slow the infection aswell. This to prevent them from getting assimilated and contribute evolution points. It is also useful to prevent [[Dispatcher (Disambiguation)|Dispatchers]] from gaining attacking units. It is particularly useful if the [[Meteor]] infection is enabled, as its impact has a chance to infect any mob within an 800 block radius, making food scarce.</ref>
*Obsidian is the block parasites can't break, and it's regarded as the best defense option. Concrete from Nuclear Tech is also good early game since most parasites can't break it and it's easy to mine from structures.
*Have a backup set of armor.
*Suicide runs to place lava on Beckons or Dispatchers is always a worthwhile measure to stop them from overgrowing and becoming too powerful. The weapons from Nuclear Tech are very much useful as well.
*An emergency bunker is also a useful tool for later phases.
*Having EMC or food farms in a far location or other dimension is a good way to make sure the parasites don't ruin everything and you process through the game without raising evolution points.
*Jetpacks are good for battling grounded and flying parasites, most notably the Overseer.
*If you see an Overseer, it's recommended to leave it alone. If there are two, DO NOT fight, SCAPE and RUN to come up with a plan. The [[Needler]] it applies is incredibly dangerous.
*Kill any parasite in Phase 0, especially Assimilated since their deaths reduce points and stop them from infecting more mobs.
*DON'T put the mod on impossible mode unless you're a god at the mod.
